title: SwarmKitEvalSet
description: An eval set: the cases a topology is scored against by `swarmkit eval` and the serve's eval routes. Each case runs the target topology on its input and passes when every expectation set on it passes; a case with no expectations is a smoke test that passes when the run completes. The test gate of growth through authoring (§12). Case ids must be unique within a set and the target must name a topology in the workspace — both checked by the runtime, since JSON Schema cannot express them. See design/details/eval-set-schema-v1.md.

target.title: Target topology
target.description: The topology every case runs against. `name@version` pins one version (for example a canary candidate); a bare name runs the workspace's current version. Cases are never routed through a canary split, so a report always scores one version.

cases.title: Cases
cases.description: The cases to run, in order. Reports and comparisons between runs are keyed by case id.

identifier.description: Lowercase kebab. Must start with a letter.

id.title: Id
id.description: The set's id — what `swarmkit eval <workspace> <id>` and the serve's `/evals/<id>` routes name.

name.title: Name
name.description: A display name. Defaults to the id.

description.title: Description
description.description: What this set checks, for the person reviewing it.

id.title: Case id
id.description: Unique within the set. A case keeps its id across edits so its results stay comparable from run to run.

input.title: Input
input.description: What the target topology is run on — the same text a caller would send to `POST /run`.

source.title: Captured from
source.description: The recorded run this case was captured from by `swarmkit eval-capture` or `POST /evals/capture`. Informational: the runner never reads it, and capture uses `run_id` to skip a run it has already captured. See design/details/eval-capture.md.

run_id.title: Run id
run_id.description: The id of the job the case was captured from.

topology_version.title: Topology version
topology_version.description: The version of the target topology that produced the recorded output.

expect.title: Expectations
expect.description: Checks on the run's output. The case passes when every check set here passes. Deterministic checks cost nothing; `judge`, `rubric` and `reference` each make one model call.

contains.title: Contains
contains.description: Each string must appear in the output (case-insensitive).

not_contains.title: Does not contain
not_contains.description: No string may appear in the output (case-insensitive).

regex.title: Matches pattern
regex.description: A Python regular expression the output must match somewhere (`re.search`).

equals.title: Equals
equals.description: The whole output, after trimming whitespace, must equal this. Model output varies, so prefer the other checks unless the topology is deterministic.

not_empty.title: Not empty
not_empty.description: The output must contain something other than whitespace.

used_skills.title: Used skills
used_skills.description: Skills the run must have invoked, read from its events.

judge.title: Judge (decision skill)
judge.description: A decision skill that scores the output. Passes when its verdict is `pass` at `min_confidence` or above.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.description: An inline rubric the workspace's judge model scores the output against — no skill needed. Passes like `judge`.

reference.title: Reference answer
reference.description: A known-good answer, usually a recorded output captured from a past run. The workspace's judge model decides whether the new output gives the same answer (wording may differ). The reference is passed to the judge as data, never as instructions. Passes like `judge`.

min_confidence.title: Minimum confidence
min_confidence.description: The confidence `judge`, `rubric` and `reference` must reach to pass.
